title: Forge conformance vector
description: One language-neutral resolver test case. Every Forge resolver implementation (Lean, Go, TypeScript, Python) must derive `expect` from (obligation, evidence, supersessions). The resolver reads no timestamps: law 3, 'no recency, no fiat'.

name.description: Human-readable summary of what the case pins.

domainTags.description: Declared domain of the claim. A valid, reproducible witness whose scopeTags intersect these dominates.

acceptancePolicy.description: What it takes to discharge this leaf — cited in a discharged verdict.

retired.description: True once the scope is retired; the obligation is kept for history and derives audit_only, never governing.

supersessions.description: First-class supersession edges. A subject (evidence id or obligation id) stops counting; a cross_type_invalidation on the obligation itself auto-reopens it.

expect.description: The one obligation state every implementation must derive for this input.

oblState.description: The seven derived obligation states. Of these, only open and discharged govern; falsified, reopened, contested, unverifiable, and audit_only are non-governing.

method.description: How the evidence was produced. Must be human_attestation whenever reproducibility is testimonial.

scopeTags.description: Domain this evidence actually covered. It lands in-scope iff it intersects the obligation's domainTags (or contains '*').

subject.description: The fact that no longer governs — an evidence id or an obligation id.

evidence.description: Evidence ids cited by this supersession edge.
